A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CheckEval. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial additions and relocation of material.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments across 12 evaluator models on SummEval and Topical-Chat, including human-score correlations, inter-evaluator agreement, and quality-stratified analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and adds QAGS evaluation, SEEval comparisons, human validation studies, and controlled supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains human-defined sub-dimensions, seed questions, independent diversification and elaboration, filtering, grouped binary evaluation, and uniform score aggregation. The prompts and seed-question tables match. Learned weighting and additional human filtering are experimental variants; v3 explicitly declines to adopt weighting in its main results.

E1.justification: v3 adds QAGS-CNN and QAGS-XSum factual-consistency evaluation, extending coverage within the existing summarization task. SummEval and Topical-Chat remain, and the new human studies use their material. Essay scoring, creative writing, and healthcare appear as cited follow-up applications, not additional evaluations conducted in this paper.

E2.justification: SEEval becomes a main comparator across the 12 evaluator models in correlation and agreement experiments. Table 10 adds reported comparisons with TIGERScore, GPTScore, Analyze-Rate, and HD-EVAL using different backbones. Appendix C additionally compares binarized and multi-sample G-Eval variants. The original main comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 changes the stated temperature from 1 to 0. The reported SummEval fluency checklist changes from 33 to 35 questions, and the Gemma2-27B checkpoint reference changes to its instruction-tuned variant; these revisions do not establish rerunning. New protocols include stratified human studies with 20 and 100 summaries, weighting learned from 20% subsets, alternative binary mappings, and three-output G-Eval aggregation.

E4.justification: v3 adds human checklist/protocol validation, additional human filtering, augmentation-removal ablation, learned-weight sensitivity analysis, output-binarization controls, and an increased-inference-budget test. These investigate validity and alternative explanations beyond v2's filtering analysis. The earlier high/low-quality analysis moves to Appendix C.1, and the naturalness case study is retained.

E5.justification: v2's Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and their p-value table are removed. v3 introduces mean and standard deviation reporting across five random seeds for weighting, significance markers for human correlations, and power-analysis-based sampling targeting a specified confidence-interval width. The main evaluation still reports n=1 and a fixed seed.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive SEEval, QAGS, human-validation, and control results. For example, Table 4 reports LLM-human checklist Spearman correlations of 0.72–0.73, while Table 22 adds Mistral-Large SEEval's Kendall correlation of 0.4962, exceeding CheckEval's retained 0.4797. Most legacy LLM scores persist. The detailed non-LLM result rows from v2 Tables 11 and 13 disappear, although their averages remain.

T1.justification: The pointwise-evaluation notation and proportion-of-yes scoring description remain equivalent. Neither version provides theorems or proofs. The added weighting and binarization experiments introduce empirical controls without new theoretical derivations or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the quantified claim of a 0.10 average improvement in correlation with humans. The introduction extends the claimed correlation advantage to SEEval as well as G-Eval. The central contributions concerning checklist evaluation, reliability, reduced model sensitivity, and interpretability remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning human agreement, residual question redundancy, unsuccessful weighting, and inference-budget effects. Appendix C.3 attributes the agreement advantage to the checklist protocol beyond output format. Its assertion of a remaining gap across all groups is overgeneralized: Table 14's Best group gives binarized G-Eval a higher Fleiss kappa than CheckEval, 0.5806 versus 0.5736. Earlier low-quality and long-text limitations remain, alongside expanded seed-design and alignment discussion.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a code-repository link, a detailed seed-writing and team-validation account, and human-study recruitment, qualifications, compensation, and annotation procedures. It adds an eight-A6000 hardware alternative and API costs for GPT-4 Turbo and GPT-4o-mini. Model-access information changes for Gemma2-27B. The existing evaluation and checklist-generation prompts are retained.

R1.justification: New citations and discussion cover SEEval, TIGERScore, Analyze-Rate, QAGS, and follow-up applications in essay, creative-writing, and healthcare evaluation. The expanded comparison clarifies the emphasis on evaluation reliability despite differing comparator backbones. The original positioning around pointwise evaluation, decomposition, and cross-model reliability remains.

P1.justification: Most introduction, related-work, method, and conclusion prose is retained. v3 revises baseline-selection explanations, moves the high/low-quality analysis and some baseline descriptions into appendices, and gives human validation a separate section. Appendix organization, author notes, terminology, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: The comparison tables expand with SEEval rows, and numerous validation, QAGS, and control tables are introduced while the significance-test table is removed. A human-validation bar chart is added and the density plot gains a SEEval curve. The unchanged quality-stratified plots and prompt figures are relocated or reordered. The detailed Topical-Chat agreement table also receives corrected dimension headers.

improvement.justification: Direct human checklist validation in Section 6 and targeted controls in Appendix C strengthen empirical scrutiny beyond v2's reliance on existing benchmark annotations and model comparisons. The net benefit is limited by removal of the main significance tests, unexplained changes in stated settings, and reporting inconsistencies. For example, SEEval's Gemma2-27B SummEval Spearman correlation is 0.44 in Table 1 but 0.4886 in Table 22, weakening confidence in parts of the expanded comparison.
